body.objective: Generalize the public Bateman--Turok finite-volume characteristic-function construction to the certified non-collinear three-particle incoming fixture and derive the complete local six-point generalized-Born detector rate.
depends_on: Bateman--Turok arXiv:2607.00096v1 Eqs. (11), (18), and Appendix B
activates: a declared dimensionless finite-volume three-to-three shell probability
a precise detector-dependence theorem for the three-particle normalization
the ten-channel compact wave-packet gluing gate
body.current_gate: Construct a permutation-symmetric finite-volume incoming characteristic cell at the exact three-beam fixture, evaluate its on-shell Jacobian and delta4(0) cancellation, carry both 3! projector factors through a symmetric outgoing cell, and combine the resulting dimension-two weight with the certified finite-time shell coefficient.
body.stop_condition: Land an exact certificate and independent verifier that reconstruct the public two-beam Area mechanism, prove idempotence and permutation counting for the declared three-beam cell, compute its regulator-dependent incoming weight and the resulting dimensionless local shell probability/rate, and keep detector independence, global channel gluing, Eq. 19, gravity, and Lorentzian causality fail-closed.
body.forbid: no coordinate-cell result called a universal three-body flux or cross section; no unsymmetrized labeled cell used as an identical-particle projector; no 3! inserted or removed without the orbit count; no finite-time shell rate called a complete S matrix; no Eq. 19, gravity, or LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL promotion
body.resource_hint: Use the exact incoming momenta kappa*(6/5,6/5,0,0), kappa*(1,-3/5,4/5,0), kappa*(1,-3/5,-4/5,0). Replace the p0x point constraint by total energy 16*kappa/5; the nine-by-nine constraint Jacobian has absolute determinant one. One ordered cell has on-shell weight 1/[8 E0 E1 E2 L0 Lx^2 Ly^3 Lz^3]. Multiplication by delta4(0)=L0 Lx Ly Lz gives 5/[48 kappa^3 Lx Ly^2 Lz^2]. Symmetric incoming and outgoing S3 orbits cancel the two 3! factors in Eq. (18).
